rv.q: The result is one of the most laugh-filled works that has ever jollied a stage
Part Monty Python, part Sherlock Holmes, this British comedy is one of New York’s funniest shows.
The current cast, for the most part, delivers the goods and, even with a reduced audience, most of the laughs still land.
It is escapist comedy at its most outrageous, so plan your escape now to New World Stages to enjoy the Off
If you haven’t witnessed the delicious disaster of That Goes Wrong, you are in for a treat.
This play, in that regard, is wholly and completely right.
It remains a master class in comic invention and execution, and in these more intimate quarters, there's a 'regular guy' element to the proceedings that closes the gap between actor and audience.
This play may have gone wrong, but when it does, it comes out deliriously right.
This reviewer found his enjoyment coming primarily from an appreciation of the comedic skills on display, rather than from the piece itself.
The pace is so relentless and the absence of anything but gags, gags, gags quickly wore out its welcome.
